title: High-Velocity Ingestion: Bulk API 2.0 vs Composite Graph API

steps.prompt: An integration job uploads 2 million Account records every weekend. It requires automatic batch chunking, parallel processing, and minimal API call overhead. Which Salesforce API should be implemented?

options.label: Bulk API 2.0 ingest job with automated server-side batch chunking
options.rationale: Bulk API 2.0 automatically slices data into optimal batches, optimizes thread concurrency on the server, and counts against daily row limits rather than individual API calls.

options.label: Composite Graph API submitted in 500-node transactional trees
options.distractorAntipattern: Composite Graph is designed for complex parent-child relational graphs under 500 nodes, not multi-million record bulk ingestion.
options.rationale: Composite Graph is limited to 500 nodes per request and 75 subrequests per graph, making 2M row ingestion inefficient and prone to payload timeouts.

options.label: REST Composite Collections API executed across concurrent workers
options.distractorAntipattern: REST Composite Collections max out at 200 records per call and consume tens of thousands of daily API allocations.
options.rationale: Ingesting 2 million records via 200-record composite calls consumes at least 10,000 API requests and risks thread contention and rate limiting.
